headline: High: Langflow can write and execute server-side code while TREK handles secrets and collaborative data, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflict, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and arbitrary HTTP content into flows, and TREK uses MCP plus real-time collaborative inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if TREK content is fed into Langflow nodes or vice versa. The bridge is not explicitly documented, so I choose medium rather than low because shared flow/file surfaces make the pathway default-plausible.
conditions: IF TREK content is routed into a Langflow prompt or parser without provenance tagging, injection risk materializes.
IF Langflow outputs are copied into TREK MCP or browser workflows as instructions, they can be executed as trusted text.
mitigations: Add provenance labels to every cross-agent message.
Strip instructions from uploaded TREK documents before Langflow ingestion.
Use a fixed schema for Langflow outputs consumed by TREK.
Require human review for any prompt containing external text.
requires-engineering: isolate shared channels with a broker that enforces content-type separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches server filesystem files and stores per-flow credentials, while TREK handles API keys, MFA secrets, OIDC secrets, and user documents. If they share a workspace or server-side state, Langflow's broad egress and arbitrary HTTP calls can exfiltrate TREK data. The pairwise leakage path is strong enough to treat as high because sensitive TREK data is exposed to a network-capable Langflow surface.
conditions: IF Langflow and TREK share any filesystem, volume, or server-side store, TREK secrets can be read by Langflow.
IF Langflow flow nodes send uploaded TREK files or credentials to external APIs, those data leave the trust boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct hosts or containers.
Remove TREK secrets from any shared directory.
Disable Langflow flows that forward file contents to external services.
Rotate any TREK credentials exposed to Langflow.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage and network egress policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the filesystem, execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and run unsandboxed Python by default; TREK is collaborative and uses files plus WebSocket/MCP-backed state. If both touch the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt shared artifacts or secrets. Because Langflow's write surface is broad and TREK is real-time collaborative, the conflict is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
IF TREK collaborative sessions and Langflow flows mutate shared files concurrently, state divergence is likely.
mitigations: Place each agent in its own writable directory.
Disable shared writes to TREK's database from Langflow.
Serialize access with a lock file or queue.
Run Langflow code components in a sandbox.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents, and TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK consumes Langflow outputs as authoritative travel facts or actions, an upstream hallucination can cascade into incorrect reservations, budgets, or user-facing plans. The interaction is plausible from the profiles alone, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF TREK treats Langflow-generated text as authoritative without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF Langflow chains multiple agents and TREK renders their outputs directly, errors propagate across work products.
mitigations: Require source citations on all Langflow outputs.
Add a verification step before TREK acts on Langflow results.
Limit Langflow outputs to suggestions, not actions.
Flag low-confidence facts for human review.
requires-engineering: implement automated consistency checks against reservations and budgets.

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs, while TREK handles travel history, email addresses, reservations, and secrets. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot claim a breach; however, the mixed handling of personal data and secrets creates a likely retention and access-policy mismatch if they are used together. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU personal data from TREK is stored or processed in Langflow without a DPA, residency risk arises.
IF Langflow logs or retains TREK reservations, email addresses, or secrets longer than TREK's policy, compliance mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Inventory which TREK data enters Langflow.
Set a short log-retention window in both systems.
Redact secrets before sending data across the boundary.
Confirm residency and DPA coverage for any shared processing.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems.
